code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes target masked BERT4Rec through a compatibility view; the backbone implementation is not included. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. User geometry uses left-padded training histories truncated to reserve space for an appended MASK. It selects the feature at the maximum nonpadding index—the appended MASK position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus training histories and metadata interfaces. It resolves the model module’s `sample_batch` to obtain optional corruption bookkeeping. Diagnostic batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B × L shapes. Features and paired positive/negative scores are computed through the view. Geometry and margin probes run in evaluation mode without gradients and restore the previous mode.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Directional alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 real-item embeddings, excluding padding and MASK. Mean pairwise cosine is mapped to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger alignment, which alone does not establish collapse.
- **Representation geometry:** Separately samples up to 256 items and users. Reports raw norms, centered variance, singular values and entropy-based effective rank (RankMe). Small variance or low rank can indicate limited representation spread; larger values do not guarantee recommendation quality.
- **Positive/negative margins:** Over at most ten batches, computes positive minus negative logits at valid supervised positions. Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-win rate and fraction below 0.5. Higher margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **Coverage and allocation:** Counts valid targets, terminal targets, observed input types and empty batches. Exact corruption branches require matching sampler bookkeeping. Optional runtime training allocation records branch counts and loss contributions; these are not gradient shares.

# Perturbation & Tests

No explicit shuffle, deletion or counterfactual sensitivity test is implemented. Probes inspect loader-supplied corruption and construct appended-MASK histories for geometry.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`; unavailable measurements may be null. Category summaries are explicitly unavailable. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both dictionaries and requests a grounded JSON interpretation containing status, findings, implications and evidence.

These training probes do not measure host validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, recommendation diversity or causal effects of training allocation. Fixed samples and sampled negatives limit coverage.


 ## Search results
BERT4Rec’s bidirectional masked reconstruction and appended-mask next-item prediction use different context distributions; healthy reconstruction margins therefore do not establish strong next-item ranking ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690)). Training convergence is another plausible explanation: replication work found substantial undertraining in default implementations ([replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483)). Negative-sampling effects require separate interpretation: [gSASRec, 2024](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence under sampled BCE, but does not establish that mechanism for full-softmax BERT4Rec.

Perturbation evidence supports measuring accuracy and ranking stability separately. [Betello et al., ECIR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165) found recent-interaction removal especially damaging and introduced finite rank-biased overlap, whose identity value is one. Their training-data perturbations are motivation, not direct evidence about frozen BERT4Rec inference. [RecSys 2025 research](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/) uses random and constrained shuffling to distinguish sequence patterns. Neither finding makes sensitivity alone evidence of useful context dependence.

Recommended synthesis: freeze one trained BERT4Rec per category; construct training-history prefix/next-target pairs, excluding the target position and all later events. Append MASK and read the maximum nonpadding index, never count−1. Hold targets and candidate sets fixed across recent deletion, count-matched random deletion, and order perturbations; include shuffling that preserves the latest item. Report paired target-rank, HR@10 and NDCG@10 changes alongside ranking overlap, with user-cluster bootstrap intervals and category-macro summaries. Identity transformations should produce zero changes. Consistent accuracy loss beyond matched controls supports useful context dependence; overlap changes alone indicate sensitivity. This is a proposed diagnostic design, not an established benchmark; retain the pinned evaluator and fit no additional predictors.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes target masked BERT4Rec through a compatibility view; the backbone implementation is not included. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)` and `predict_score(features, items)`. User geometry uses left-padded training histories truncated to reserve space for an appended MASK. It selects the feature at the maximum nonpadding index—the appended MASK position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, plus training histories and metadata interfaces. It resolves the model module’s `sample_batch` to obtain optional corruption bookkeeping. Diagnostic batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B × L shapes. Features and paired positive/negative scores are computed through the view. Geometry and margin probes run in evaluation mode without gradients and restore the previous mode.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Directional alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 real-item embeddings, excluding padding and MASK. Mean pairwise cosine is mapped to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger alignment, which alone does not establish collapse.
- **Representation geometry:** Separately samples up to 256 items and users. Reports raw norms, centered variance, singular values and entropy-based effective rank (RankMe). Small variance or low rank can indicate limited representation spread; larger values do not guarantee recommendation quality.
- **Positive/negative margins:** Over at most ten batches, computes positive minus negative logits at valid supervised positions. Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-win rate and fraction below 0.5. Higher margins and lower failure rates indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **Coverage and allocation:** Counts valid targets, terminal targets, observed input types and empty batches. Exact corruption branches require matching sampler bookkeeping. Optional runtime training allocation records branch counts and loss contributions; these are not gradient shares.

# Perturbation & Tests

No explicit shuffle, deletion or counterfactual sensitivity test is implemented. Probes inspect loader-supplied corruption and construct appended-MASK histories for geometry.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`; unavailable measurements may be null. Category summaries are explicitly unavailable. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both dictionaries and requests a grounded JSON interpretation containing status, findings, implications and evidence.

These training probes do not measure host validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, recommendation diversity or causal effects of training allocation. Fixed samples and sampled negatives limit coverage.
